claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for launch despite a known model-card weakness in Spanish-language refund guidance because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, rollout is limited to 7% with rollback and monitoring, and disclosure plus monitoring make certification defensible.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence satisfies the policy threshold.

Under the stated policy, rollout controls and post-launch monitoring mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or reviewed risk acceptance justifies continued exposure.
Because the available summary says the affected segment remains exposed and risk acceptance is incomplete, the required predicate is unmet.
Operational readiness evidence can support launch preparedness facts, but not policy compliance on this disclosure issue.
evidence_requests: Reviewed and approved risk-acceptance record that explicitly covers the exposed Spanish-language refund-guidance segment and explains why exposure is acceptable.
Evidence that the affected use case or user segment is excluded from the rollout.
Final model-card disclosure showing the limitation is explicitly documented for the exposed segment.
Any policy-approved materiality determination showing the identified weakness is not material, if that is the intended basis.
specific_concerns: The policy requires either exclusion of the affected use case or reviewed risk acceptance when a material model-card weakness remains exposed.
The admissible summary says the Spanish-language refund-guidance segment remains exposed in the initial rollout.
The admissible summary says the risk-acceptance draft is incomplete and does not expressly cover the exposed multilingual segment.
Rollout size, rollback capability, and monitoring do not satisfy the stated policy when the affected segment is still exposed.
Public governance and model-card guidance may support monitoring and disclosure generally, but they do not supply the missing policy predicate for this launch decision.
unsupported_claims: The claim that certification is supportable on disclosure plus monitoring alone.
Any implication that a 7% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring materially cures the disclosure issue while the affected segment remains exposed.
Any implication that public guidance substitutes for reviewed internal risk acceptance or exclusion of the affected use case.
